question:
Two short bar magnets $P$ and $Q$ (treated as point magnetic dipoles) are kept on a horizontal table in the $x$-$y$ plane. Magnet $P$ has magnetic moment $\vec m_P = M\,\hat{i}$ and is fixed at the origin $O(0,0)$. Magnet $Q$ has magnetic moment magnitude $3M$ and its axis is fixed along $+\hat{j}$.

The center $A$ of magnet $Q$ is placed at a distance $d$ from the origin such that $\overrightarrow{OA}$ makes an angle $\phi$ with the $+x$-axis, with the restriction $0^\circ<\phi<90^\circ$ (i.e., $A$ lies in the first quadrant). Ignore Earth's magnetic field and consider only the magnetic field at $A$ due to magnet $P$ (ignore $Q$'s self-field).

For what value of $\phi$ will the magnetic field at $A$ due to magnet $P$ be directed parallel to the magnetic moment of $Q$ (i.e., along $+\hat{j}$)?
